newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Intria says expects to get rail job soon.
newsitem.headline: Intria says expects to get rail job soon.

text.p: Malaysian infrastructure developer Intria Bhd said on Wednesday it expected to receive approval some time in February to participate in a 1.7 billion-ringgit rail project near Kuala Lumpur.

"Not many companies have the expertise to undertake such a project, and we propose to complete this mammoth construction 24 months from the date of the approval, which is expected some time this month," said Intria chairman Azman Firdaus Shafii in an interview with the national news agency Bernama.

The project would involve the construction of a dedicated high speed rail link between central Kuala Lumpur and the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport, which is being built about 50 km (30 miles) outside the capital.
Intria acquired a 40 percent stake in British construction company Costain Plc in July, saving it from major financial losses.
"We want to...offer both Intria's and Costain's services in view of the project's complexities," Bernama quoted Azman as saying.
He said the project would be carried out using contractors belonging to Tabung Haji Technologies Sdn Bhd.
"The tie-up between Intria and Costain has ensured a transfer of technology to Malaysians," said Azman.

Azman added that the two companies were joining forces to become the engineering, procurement and construction contractor to bid for a five-billion-ringgit, 2,000-megawatt power station for national power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd in the northern Malaysian town of Lumut.

In October, the Public Works Ministry asked Intria's parent company, Mekar Idaman Sdn Bhd, to submit a proposal to build additional lanes on the Penang Bridge, Asia's longest. The bridge links northern Penang island and the Malaysian mainland.
Officials at Intria and Costain could not be immediately reached for comment.
